summary: Describes extensions to GMPLS signaling needed to control Optical Transport Networks defined by G.709, including pre-OTN developments. It is a companion to the GMPLS signaling documents and is on the standards track.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 4328 extends GMPLS signaling so routers can request paths through G.709 optical transport networks. A request identifies the signal type, how it is combined with other signals, and the slot or wavelength to use.

subtitle: Signaling extensions for setting up paths through G.709 optical transport networks.

tldr.problem: GMPLS signaling needed to describe G.709 optical and digital transport paths, including multiplexed signals and their positions within larger signals.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC adds encoding and payload identifiers, traffic parameters for signal type and composition, and labels that identify ODU tributary slots.
tldr.outcome: RFC 4328 extends GMPLS signaling for G.709, updates RFC 3471, and was later updated by RFC 7139.

today: RFC 4328 is a Proposed Standard published in January 2006. It updates RFC 3471 and was later updated by RFC 7139.

sections.title: G.709 Layers and GMPLS
sections.content:
G.709 defines optical transport layers and digital layers. The Optical Channel (OCh) and Optical Channel Data Unit (ODUk) are switching layers. Smaller ODU signals can be multiplexed into larger ODU signals.

RFC 4328 extends GMPLS to signal paths at the ODUk digital layer and OCh optical layer. It defines an ODU label space as a tree: the root is an OTUk signal and the leaves identify ODU signals carried within it.
sections.plainLanguage: G.709 signals can be carried inside larger signals. GMPLS needs to identify both the type of signal and where it fits in the larger one.

sections.title: Encoding and Payload Identifiers
sections.content:
The Generalized Label Request gains LSP Encoding Type value 12 for G.709 ODUk and value 13 for G.709 Optical Channel. A node that cannot support a requested encoding must return a PathErr. No new Switching Type is needed: ODUk uses the TDM class and OCh uses the Lambda class.

The Generalized-PID identifies the client payload carried by the path. RFC 4328 adds values 47 through 58 for payloads including ODUj, OTUk, bit streams, IP/PPP, Ethernet, ESCON, FICON and Fiber Channel.
sections.plainLanguage: A path request says which optical layer it uses and what data it carries. New number values identify G.709 layers and payload types.

sections.title: Signal Type and Traffic Parameters
sections.content:
G.709 traffic parameters identify the signal type, number of multiplexed components (NMC), number of virtual components (NVC), and multiplier (MT). Signal Type values 1, 2 and 3 identify ODU1, ODU2 and ODU3; values 6, 7 and 8 identify OCh at the listed rates.

NMC describes tributary slots used by a multiplexed ODU signal. NVC describes identical signals joined by virtual concatenation. MT requests identical copies of a signal and must not be zero. The RFC applies virtual concatenation before multiplication.
sections.plainLanguage: The request lists the signal, how many slots it uses, whether signals are joined, and how many copies are needed. Devices check that they can support those values.

sections.title: Labels for ODU Signals
sections.content:
An ODUk label is a 32-bit value with fields t3, t2 and t1. Together they identify whether the selected signal is an ODU1, ODU2 or ODU3 and, when multiplexed, which tributary slot it uses.

For an ODU2 multiplexed into an ODU3, four labels identify the four tributary slots. Label values are sent in an ordered list, and the order reflects the signal components rather than the physical order of slots. An all-zero label is invalid.
sections.plainLanguage: The label is an address inside a larger optical signal. Its fields identify the signal level and the slot that carries it.

sections.title: Distributing Labels and Signaling Traffic
sections.content:
The Generalized Label carries one 32-bit value for an ODUk mapped directly into an OTUk. Multiplexing, virtual concatenation or multiplication can require an ordered list of labels. The traffic parameters travel in G.709 SENDER_TSPEC and FLOWSPEC objects.

Intermediate and egress nodes check whether they support the requested signal type, NMC and NVC. If they do not, they return a PathErr. A zero multiplier is invalid and also requires a PathErr.
sections.plainLanguage: The response returns one label for a single signal or a list when the request uses several components. A node reports an error if it cannot support the requested signal.

fields.name: Signal Type
fields.desc: Identifies the elementary ODU or OCh signal.

fields.name: Multiplier
fields.desc: Number of identical signals; zero is invalid.
